note: Six Rivers NF campground in Douglas fir on Hwy 199 at the confluence of Patrick Creek and the Middle Fork Smith River, with CCC-built stone steps, walls and fire circles. The sites sit on a flat about 30 ft above the river; short trails lead down to a fishing platform and a small sandy beach. Sites 4, 6, 8, 12 and 13 are first-come. --Claude
summary: rec.gov API + catalog + availability + FS page + imagery read. 13 sites (8 reservable, 5 walk-up), RV 30-45 ft; no hookups; flush toilets + drinking water (FS says no potable water - flag); $14 + $5 extra vehicle (one extra max); season ~May 18 - Sep 14 (2026; was unknown), closed now (seasonal). Not waterfront kept (sites 30 ft above the river over a vertical bank; river creek-size at the camp) - lead given. Phone '' -> 707-457-3131. Pin OK (~30 m).
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (not waterfront kept): FS page: 'The campsites are situated on a flat about 30 feet above the river. From the campground, the river can only be viewed from sites 7, 8, 9, and 12 looking down over a fence and vertical bank.' Imagery (Esri, 41.8717,-123.8477): the Middle Fork Smith's summer wetted channel by the south-row sites is ~15 m (~25 m with the gravel bar), so it is creek-size at the camp (<30 m); creekside fails on the ~9 m vertical bank (no easy walk down from the sites; access is by short trails). If AWH counts the Middle Fork as a river, sites 7, 8, 9 and 12 (all bookable, 38-45 ft; 8 and 12 first-come) would support riverview. Suggested evidence: 'FS page 2026-11-27: sites on a flat ~30 ft above the river, river seen only from 7, 8, 9, 12 down a fence and vertical bank; Esri: wetted channel ~15 m at the camp -> creek-size, bank fails creekside -> not waterfront.'
